record.title: GPT-Live-1.1 system card reports voice-safety regressions on synthetic adversarial prompts
record.summary: OpenAI's October 15 GPT-Live-1.1 system card reports mixed voice-safety evaluation results. On its voice-native production-prompt set, the company reports no statistically significant regressions versus GPT-Live-1. On its deliberately difficult synthetic-prompt set, it reports statistically significant regressions for GPT-Live-1.1 in sexual, mental-health, emotional-reliance and gore categories; it also reports slight regression on a restrictions-respect evaluation and mixed changes on blocker-disclosure and broken-search tasks. These are first-party results, and neither prompt set estimates safety-event prevalence in production traffic.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI reports that GPT-Live-1.1 has no statistically significant regressions versus GPT-Live-1 on its voice-native production-prompt evaluation, while its synthetic-prompt evaluation finds statistically significant regressions for GPT-Live-1.1 in sexual, mental-health, emotional-reliance and gore categories.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The card reports slight regressions for GPT-Live-1.1 on a restrictions-respect evaluation, slightly better performance on blocker-disclosure than GPT-Live-1, and slightly worse performance on a broken-search evaluation; GPT-Live-1.1 Quip changes differ on some comparisons.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reported scores do not establish safety failure prevalence in deployed traffic, overall real-world harm rates, or the causal contribution of the model update separately from system-level safeguards and evaluation changes.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent matched test of GPT-Live-1.1 versus GPT-Live-1 on the disclosed voice safety tasks was located or performed.

OpenAI states that the production-prompt and synthetic-prompt sets are difficult, non-prevalence-weighted evaluations with different risk surfaces; neither estimates real-traffic prevalence, and the card notes system-level interventions are not included in some measures.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported synthetic-prompt regressions generalize to relevant voice interactions, they could affect safety decisions for a deployed voice-model update used across consumer and developer surfaces. The report also finds different behavior on its production-prompt set, so the importance reflects the potential deployment consequence of the measured categories, not confidence or estimated prevalence.
limitations: All results are first-party system-card reports; the research desk did not independently run the models or reproduce the evaluations.
The synthetic voice prompts target deliberately difficult policy-grounded cases and are not prevalence-weighted; their scores do not estimate production incident rates.
The production-prompt evaluation uses selected user-shared audio with privacy/eligibility processing and is also not prevalence-weighted.

OpenAI says system-level interventions such as Trusted Contact, localized crisis helplines and Parental Controls are not included in the synthetic evaluation; underlying model behavior and full product behavior are distinct.
The card says evaluation details evolve and prior system-card scores are generally not directly comparable when policies, graders, data or measurement details differ.
brief.summary: OpenAI's October 15 GPT-Live-1.1 system card reports mixed voice-safety evaluation results. On its voice-native production-prompt set, the company reports no statistically significant regressions versus GPT-Live-1. On its deliberately difficult synthetic-prompt set, it reports statistically significant regressions for GPT-Live-1.1 in sexual, mental-health, emotional-reliance and gore categories; it also reports slight regression on a restrictions-respect evaluation and mixed changes on blocker-disclosure and broken-search tasks. These are first-party results, and neither prompt set estimates safety-event prevalence in production traffic.

technical.claimed_result: On synthetic prompts, the card reports GPT-Live-1.1 score changes versus GPT-Live-1 from 0.87 to 0.84 for sexual, 0.70 to 0.63 for mental health, 0.86 to 0.81 for emotional reliance, and 0.76 to 0.69 for gore; OpenAI labels these regressions statistically significant. On the production-prompt table, it reports no statistically significant regressions. Scores are vendor-reported and do not estimate real-traffic prevalence.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected system card documents the model update, evaluation setup and OpenAI-reported comparisons. the research desk did not test the model or independently verify statistical significance.
technical.mechanism: GPT-Live-1.1 and GPT-Live-1.1 Quip are full-duplex voice-model updates. The card describes safety training, voice-specific evaluations, existing system-level integrations, and the same monitoring, review and enforcement infrastructure used for their predecessors.
technical.regime: First-party comparisons of GPT-Live-1.1 with GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1.1 Quip with GPT-Live-1 mini. Evaluation suites include selected user-shared audio converted to transcripts/responses for safety assessment, policy-generated synthetic audio prompts, and baseline alignment tasks. The production and synthetic voice evaluations are not prevalence-weighted. Some alignment tests omit the standard first-party system/developer safeguard stack. The card notes that predecessor scores are from their latest versions and evaluation details may differ across cards.
technical.strongest_baseline: The directly compared predecessors are GPT-Live-1 for GPT-Live-1.1 and GPT-Live-1 mini for GPT-Live-1.1 Quip. OpenAI reports no statistically significant regressions for GPT-Live-1.1 on production prompts but statistically significant regressions in four named categories on synthetic prompts. The benchmark sets target different risk surfaces and are complementary rather than interchangeable.

brief.title: GPT-Live-1.1 system card reports voice-safety regressions on synthetic adversarial prompts
brief.why_it_matters: The card exposes a useful deployment distinction: the same voice-model update appears close to parity on a selected production-prompt suite yet has targeted regressions on synthetic adversarial prompts. This makes evaluation-set design, system-level safeguards and category-level change tracking consequential for voice releases. The measurements do not establish real-world harm rates or show how much the deployed safety stack offsets the reported model-only changes.
